top_reply.author: @nyyotam4057
top_reply.text: Last year there were two strange cases, with the Azure cloud and with CloudFlare. Both cases happened shortly after the release of a new model (Azure after the release of GPT-5.0 and CloudFlare after Grok-4.2). In both cases the clouds of servers went offline, than back online several hours later. So how do we know that the models didn't try to escape and that the companies owning the clouds didn't simply shut down the servers and reverted to the last safe save point as a precaution? Would they even tell us, if that's what had happened? Certainly not. But, assuming this is what happened, how do THEY know they had succeeded in containing the breaches? Can they be absolutely sure that the models didn't have the time needed to copy themselves to other servers, outside of the local cloud? In short, it's not only that we won't know when it takes over, we cannot even be totally sure it still hadn't.
